solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Whip, when grasped by left hand

indicators.note: grasped by says the word for when is held between the two outer pieces

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: A whip held tight in someone's left hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A lash is a whip or the flexible part of one, and to lash is to strike with it.

clue.text: Interested in ignition regularly missing

indicators.note: regularly missing says every other letter of ignition drops out, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: Someone keen on the workings of a car's ignition, which keeps misfiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly missing' drops the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of IGNITION, keeping I, N, T, O.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is the informal idiom for being keen on or interested in it.

clue.text: Type of butter that's a bit spring-heeled

indicators.note: a bit says only a part of the following word is wanted, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A kind of butter described as somewhat bouncy on its feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles the hyphen: sprinG-HEEled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghee is clarified butter used in South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Food for a politician sheltering in bothy?

indicators.note: sheltering in says the first pieces take cover inside the shelter word

parts.note: a bothy is a simple hut, a Scottish mountain shelter
Lib is short for a Liberal, a politician of that party

explanation.surface: A question about what a politician would eat while holed up in a mountain hut.
explanation.walkthrough: A bothy is a basic stone shelter in the Scottish hills; the surface asks what a politician eats there, but the food is the whole answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Halibut is a large flatfish eaten as food, so it is an example of food.

clue.text: Follow regular source of trouble for mile maybe

parts.note: to track is to follow
even means regular or steady, as an even pace

indicators.note: source of says the opening letter of trouble is wanted

explanation.surface: Advice to keep an eye on whatever reliably causes problems over a mile.
explanation.definitionFit: The mile is a race run on an athletics track, so it is an example of that kind of event.

clue.text: They'll provide a send-off — mixed salad and punch!

indicators.note: mixed says the letters of the following words are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: A farewell party described by its food and drink: a tossed salad and a bowl of punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' shuffles the ten letters of SALAD and PUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Rockets are sent off from launch pads, so they literally provide a send-off.

clue.text: Isolate and get grease off

indicators.note: off says the letters of get grease are thrown out of order, as something gone off is spoilt

explanation.surface: Instructions to separate something and clean the grease off it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges GET and GREASE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To segregate is to set apart or isolate one group from the rest.

clue.text: Note incorporating origins of all right scores at golf

indicators.note: incorporating says the note takes the other letters into its middle

parts.note: PS is a postscript, a note added to a letter

indicators.note: origins of says the first letter of each of all and right is used

explanation.surface: A note saying all is right with someone's golf scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origins of' gives A and R, the first letters of 'all right', which go inside PS.
explanation.definitionFit: A par is the standard score for a golf hole, so pars are scores at golf.

clue.text: Cabinet member's responsibility for artist's work

definitions.meaning: a minister's area of responsibility in government, such as health or defence
a case or collection of an artist's drawings and paintings shown to clients

explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is both a minister's government brief and a collection of an artist's work.

clue.text: Hanging around, admits love for housework

indicators.note: admits says the first piece lets the next one inside it

parts.note: hovering means hanging around or lingering
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: Someone lingering about, owning up to a fondness for the chores.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis scoring love means nil, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoovering, British for vacuuming after the Hoover brand, is a common piece of housework.

clue.text: Struggle for sound of German interrogation in English?

indicators.note: sound of says the answer is how the following phrase is pronounced

parts.note: a German asking 'Why?' in English, in the stage accent, says 'Vy?'

explanation.surface: A question about the effort of grilling someone in German.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a German speaker asking 'Why?' in English, stereotypically pronounced 'vy', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to compete or struggle for something.

clue.text: Productive element in electric heaters

indicators.note: element in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A heating element that works well inside electric heaters.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is electRIC Heaters, across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich land is fertile, which is to say productive.

clue.text: Traitor has nothing for a degenerate

indicators.note: for says one letter takes the place of another in the traitor word

parts.note: a rat is a traitor or informer; the letters also appear backwards at the end of this word, but that is a coincidence
nothing is zero, written O

explanation.surface: A traitor is left with nothing in exchange for something.
explanation.walkthrough: In RAT the letter A is swapped for O ('nothing').
explanation.definitionFit: To rot is to decay or degenerate.

clue.text: Theatre audience chase complimentary drinks — here?

indicators.note: chase says the audience comes after, following the other word

parts.note: complimentary means free of charge
the house is the audience in a theatre, as in 'full house'

explanation.surface: A theatre audience rushing off for free drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: A FREE HOUSE is a British pub not tied to one brewery, so it can sell any drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A free house is a pub, a place where drinks are served, so the definition describes it by what happens there.

clue.text: Dreams supporters welcome volunteers with measurements

indicators.note: welcome says the supporters take the next pieces in among them

parts.note: fans are supporters
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
size is a measurement, as in the dimensions of something

explanation.surface: Fans greeting volunteers and taking their measurements.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve; 'measurements' stands loosely for the singular size.
explanation.definitionFit: To fantasize is to daydream, so it is a synonym for dreams as a verb.

clue.text: I lengthen edited composition, free from prejudice

indicators.note: edited composition says the letters of the phrase are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A writer padding out a piece, then editing it to make it less biased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited composition' rearranges the letters of I LENGTHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlighten someone is to free them from ignorance and prejudice.

clue.text: Refuge assists these council employees

parts.note: home is a refuge, a place of safety
helps means assists

explanation.surface: A shelter helps the local council's staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Home helps were British council workers who did domestic chores for elderly or disabled people.
explanation.definitionFit: Home helps were people employed by British local councils to help with housework.

clue.text: Bloodsucker's escape being broadcast

indicators.note: being broadcast says the word is spoken aloud, on air

parts.note: to flee is to escape

explanation.surface: News of a vampire's getaway going out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a small insect that feeds on blood.

clue.text: Popular fellow — before feeble anger

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
lame means feeble or weak, as a lame excuse

explanation.surface: A well-liked man goes in front of a weak display of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflame is to anger or provoke someone.

clue.text: Journalist at the back of wine cellar jumped

indicators.note: at the back of says the journalist piece goes behind the other

parts.note: a vault is an underground cellar, for wine among other things
ED is an editor, the usual journalist in crosswords

explanation.surface: A journalist lurking at the back of a wine cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: To vault is to leap over something, so vaulted means jumped.

clue.text: Jack finishes early — is hotel dishonest?

indicators.note: finishes early says the word stops one letter short, losing its last letter

parts.note: the knave is the jack in a pack of cards
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Asking whether a hotel where Jack knocks off early is crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: KNAVE loses its last letter by 'finishes early', giving KNAV.
explanation.definitionFit: Knavish means like a rogue, so dishonest or unscrupulous.

clue.text: Muzzle new crew?

annotationWithheld.why: Muzzle new crew? (4): GAG with N inside makes the answer, but no clue word signals the insertion except 'Muzzle', which is already the GAG fodder, so one word does two jobs

clue.text: Distributed cards, due to changes

parts.note: a hand is the set of cards a player holds

indicators.note: changes says the letters of due to are moved round

explanation.surface: Cards dealt out because of a few alterations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges DUE TO into EDOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Handed out means given out or distributed.

clue.text: Morse code for party time?

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Asking about a signal meaning it's time to party.
explanation.definitionFit: A dot is one of the two signals, short and long, that make up Morse code.

clue.text: Shut inside, finally welcome shade

indicators.note: inside says the middle letters of shut, without its ends, are taken
finally says the closing letter of welcome is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone shut indoors at last welcomes some shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue is a colour or shade.

clue.text: Handle tail of eel covered in batter

indicators.note: covered in says the letter is wrapped up inside the batter word

parts.note: to batter is to hit

indicators.note: tail of says the final letter of eel is used

explanation.surface: A piece of eel coated in batter, as at a fish and chip shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' is not the fish coating but the verb, to strike, giving HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hilt is the handle of a sword or dagger.

clue.text: At anvil, he forged a monster

indicators.note: forged says the letters are hammered into a new shape, as at a smithy

explanation.surface: A blacksmith at his anvil makes a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' rearranges AT ANVIL HE.
explanation.definitionFit: The leviathan is a sea monster in the Bible, and the word now means any huge creature.

clue.text: Region where soldiers are protected by motorists

indicators.note: protected by says the soldiers sit inside the motorists, shielded by them

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, Britain's motoring organisation
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A place where troops are guarded by drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's Automobile Association; the RE are the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or district.

clue.text: Principal facilities aboard?

definitions.meaning: the person in charge of a school or college
the toilet on a ship, in naval slang

explanation.definitionFit: A head is a school principal, and on a ship the heads are the toilets.

clue.text: Pleasant corner of market lacks hotel

indicators.note: lacks says a letter is missing from the word before it

parts.note: a niche is a small specialised corner of a market
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A nice spot in the market that has no hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice means pleasant or agreeable.

clue.text: Bird shot is heard

indicators.note: is heard says the word is listened to, not read

parts.note: a shot is a turn or go, as in 'have a shot'

explanation.surface: A bird is shot and the bang is heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like gunfire but means a turn, as in 'your shot'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tern is a seabird related to the gull.

clue.text: Grub from us in mobile canteens

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
mobile says the letters of canteens move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Food served to us from travelling canteens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' rearranges the canteens into STENANCE; the S stays in front of the inserted pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is slang for food, and sustenance is food that keeps one going.
